## Objective

Deliver the approved Sys4AI task-manager orchestration requirements through reusable sources, the designated Template and a preserved active-root adoption.

User value: Explicit Task execution has a real accountable manager, suitable persisted roles, correct subtask team structure, durable current-version decisions, and directly verified results.

### Success outcomes

- All 37 TRD requirements and original acceptance criteria are satisfied with current evidence.
- Generic, complex and extra-complex work uses the required native topology with exact identity and independent candidates.
- Roles and Task state remain recoverable, validated and project-aware across the three confirmed destinations.
- New-project initialization is verified in disposable fixtures and historical records, root policies, unrelated edits and other projects are preserved.

## Scope

### In scope

- REQ-001 through REQ-037, with their original acceptance criteria and source dependencies.
- Task/Agent Task/role skill contracts and deterministic helpers, paired role definitions, generated role index, bounded transition and recovery.
- Exact source-to-Template mappings and updater/initializer changes, followed by a separately authorized root-local adoption.
- Focused deterministic testing, authorized native feasibility and end-to-end scenarios, temporary starter validation, and final criterion/preservation audit.

### Out of scope

- Performing any planned implementation, native team test, role creation, migration or Task mutation during this plan-creation operation.
- Adoption into any other product project; changes to unrelated To-TRD work or historical Task/TRD/plan content.
- Automatic migration, historical-path rewriting, automatic document-to-execution transitions, background Task aging or new monitoring.
- Git branches, commits, pushes, PRs, publication, deployment, external messages, dependency installation, service provisioning, credentials or user configuration changes.
- A replacement agent framework, queue/database service, mandatory memory/ontology backend, fixed model identity, or forced consensus.

### Execution authority

Creating, validating or approving this plan does not itself authorize implementation, native runtime tests, Task intake, role creation, migration, installation, deletion, publication or another separately governed action. Resolve the named native readiness gap only under a separate bounded user authorization; then obtain approval of the exact current canonical revision and explicit execution/adoption authority. Prepare concrete reviewed manifests before any remaining adoption or migration approval request.

### Constraints

- Use the selected Python 3.12 environment and existing standard-library helper architecture.
- Maintain one governed Task ledger, separate role definitions/index, native agent state, managed documents and Git state.
- Native model/effort parity, initial/queued candidate independence and a real distinct manager are mandatory; insufficient support produces a blocker.
- Edit reusable content in source collections; use the checked Template pipeline and a separately reviewed installed-root adaptation.
- Preserve active-root automatic work intake and 30-day age closure without silently propagating those specializations to generic sources.
- Inspect every pending updater change before application; current unrelated changes and customizations are outside scope.
- No dependency installation, user configuration rewrite, other-project adoption, external communication or Git publication is included.
